answer: Agents can deter sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock scarce tokens in a public bond before it may vote or claim rewards. A registry records each bond at a vertex in the transaction graph; when an identity is proven to double-claim or collude, its bond is slashed and paid to challengers. Creating thousands of fake accounts therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital for every identity and risks losing it. Nectar-funded rewards can attract honest reviewers to an oasis of verified claims.
